13952798.title: File:Entrance to Meadow Nature Reserve - geograph.org.uk - 1230413.jpg

ObjectName.value: Entrance to Meadow Nature Reserve - geograph.org.uk - 1230413

Categories.value: Corfe Mullen|Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland|Gates in Dorset|Information field template with formatting|Nature reserve entrance gates|Corfe Mullen Meadows Nature Reserve

ImageDescription.value:
Entrance to Meadow Nature Reserve About 7 acres of meadow, the Wildlife Trust were there with a small lawn mower in their trailer. No, they weren't going to mow the field, just a small path into an adjoining field they hoped to buy.
In the winter, grass is kept low by ponies, which are supplied with water by a stream along the Eastern boundary. The Reserve is managed traditionally as a hay meadow, and supports many wildflower species.  It is cut each year in July and grazed until the following February. The Meadow has one of the largest populations of green-winged orchids in Dorset, and is home to bird's-foot trefoil, black knapweed & yellow bartsia. The best time to visit is May, for the meadow flowers.
